title: Linking through JWT unique identifier
description: JWT tokens contain unique identifiers that can link data across systems and sessions, potentially enabling tracking of user activities across different contexts.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted in clear or can be intercepted

title: Identified information in JWT
description: JWT tokens contain user identity information that directly identifies the data subject, enabling identification of the parent user from the token data.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims

title: Quasi-identifiers in user data
description: User data transmitted alongside JWT may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., email, role, permissions) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify the data subject.
assumptions: User data includes multiple attributes that can be combined for identification

title: Potentially sensitive data types transmitted
description: User data transmitted to parent user may include sensitive information beyond what is functionally required for the authentication service interaction.
assumptions: User data may contain sensitive attributes not needed for parent user context

title: Data propagation to parent user
description: Personal data is propagated from authentication service to parent user, potentially exposing data to parties where it may not be functionally needed.
assumptions: Parent user may not require all transmitted data

title: Unawareness of data transmission
description: Parent user may not be fully aware of what personal data is being transmitted from the authentication service and how it will be used.
assumptions: User consent or awareness mechanisms may be insufficient

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Transmission of user data alongside JWT may process more personal data than functionally required for the authentication service interaction.
assumptions: Data minimization principle requires only necessary data to be transmitted

title: Linking through parent email identifier
description: Parent email serves as a unique identifier that can link the child's login activity to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the child's usage patterns to the parent or third parties.
assumptions: Email addresses are typically unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combination through email and password
description: The combination of parent email and password can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow linking of login sessions to specific individuals.
assumptions: Email+password combination may be unique enough for identification

title: Processing of identified data during child login
description: The authentication service processes identified personal data (parent email and password) during the child login process, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Email and password are clearly identifiable personal data

title: Email as unique identifier for data subject
description: Parent email contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (parent), which is processed during child authentication.
assumptions: Email addresses are unique identifiers

title: Collection of highly sensitive password data
description: Password is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required. The system collects and processes password data during authentication.
assumptions: Passwords are among the most sensitive personal data types

title: Unnecessary processing of password data
description: Password data is processed for authentication purposes, but the extent of processing (storage, hashing, etc.) may exceed what is functionally needed for the login functionality.
assumptions: Password processing may include unnecessary transformations

title: Child unawareness of data processing implications
description: The child user may not be fully aware of the implications of using parent credentials for their own login, including data collection and processing.
assumptions: Children may lack understanding of privacy implications

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The child user has limited control over how their parent's data is processed, stored, and potentially shared during the authentication process.
assumptions: Children typically have limited privacy controls

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing parent email and password for child login may process more personal data than functionally necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle requires processing only necessary data

title: Potential invalid consent for child data processing
description: A child's consent for processing parent credentials may be invalid or questionable, as children typically lack legal capacity to provide valid consent.
assumptions: Children may not have legal capacity to consent to data processing

title: Linking through unique user identifiers
description: Child User identifiers are used to link video search queries, likes, and comments to specific individuals, enabling cross-context linking of user activities.
assumptions: User accounts maintain persistent identifiers across interactions

title: Profiling individual through video behavior
description: Video Management Service analyzes video search patterns, likes, and comments to build profiles of individual users' interests and preferences.
assumptions: System collects and analyzes behavioral data for personalization

title: Processing of identified user data
description: The system requests and processes identified data including user IDs associated with video search, requests, likes, and comments.
assumptions: User authentication and identification is required for all interactions

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content, search queries, and comments may contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: User-generated content may include personal or identifying information

title: Attributable data evidence from user actions
description: Video search, requests, likes, and comments can be attributed to specific users, preventing denial of these actions.
assumptions: All user actions are logged and associated with user accounts

title: Detection through observed communications
description: Video search queries and interactions can be observed and detected by the system or third parties.
assumptions: System logs and monitors all user interactions

title: Collection of sensitive video data
description: Video content may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic video management functionality.
assumptions: Video data collection exceeds minimum functional requirements

title: Unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: Video data may be further analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is necessary for the stated functionality.
assumptions: System performs additional processing on video data for analytics or personalization

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Child Users may not be fully aware of the extent of data collection, processing, and storage of their video interactions.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data processing activities

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms and preference settings may be limited or unclear

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed for the video management functionality.
assumptions: System collects and processes data beyond functional requirements

title: Potential invalid consent for data processing
description: Personal data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent from data subjects.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not meet legal standards for validity

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for streaming approved video to a child.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: Video data may be streamed at a finer granularity than necessary, potentially revealing more personal details than required for the child viewing.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be processed, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is needed to achieve the functional goal of streaming approved video to a child.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (the child), which may be more than functionally necessary.

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The system processes identified video data that can be associated with specific individuals.

title: Revealing attributes in video
description: Video data may contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject, such as facial features, location, or activities.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in video
description: Video data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., location, time, activity patterns) that can be combined to link data to specific individuals.

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Video data can be analyzed for patterns to link data to specific individuals or infer personal characteristics.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: The child data subject may not be fully aware of the collection, processing, or streaming of their video data.

title: Lack of control over video preferences
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed and streamed.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data may be processed beyond what is actually needed, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.

title: Potential invalid consent for video processing
description: Video data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent from the child or their guardians.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, cookies, user IDs) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across different contexts.
assumptions: Browsing data collection includes identifier tracking mechanisms

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Browsing data contains multiple quasi-identifiers (IP address, device type, browsing patterns, timestamps) that when combined can uniquely identify individuals.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to sufficient quasi-identifiers to perform re-identification

title: Profiling an individual through browsing behavior
description: Advertisers can analyze browsing data patterns to build profiles of individuals, linking browsing behavior to personal characteristics and preferences.
assumptions: Advertisers perform behavioral analysis on received browsing data

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: Browsing data may contain direct identifiers or unique references that allow identification of the data subject when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Browsing data collection includes user identification mechanisms

title: Revealing attributes in browsing data
description: Browsing data reveals sensitive attributes about users including interests, location patterns, and behavioral characteristics that support identification.
assumptions: Browsing data includes detailed behavioral and contextual information

title: Data propagation to third-party advertisers
description: Browsing data is propagated from the AI Recommendation Engine to external third-party advertisers beyond what may be functionally necessary for the core recommendation functionality.
assumptions: Data sharing with advertisers is not strictly required for the AI recommendation engine's primary function

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Browsing data is shared with a predetermined set of third-party advertisers, expanding the exposure of personal data beyond the immediate system boundary.
assumptions: Advertiser relationships are established and fixed at design time

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected and shared with third-party advertisers for advertising purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate data sharing with advertisers

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack meaningful control over how their browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers, including inability to opt-out or customize sharing preferences.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms for data sharing may be unclear or difficult to exercise

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Browsing data shared with advertisers may exceed what is functionally necessary for the stated purpose, potentially including more detailed or extensive data than required.
assumptions: Data sharing agreements may not enforce strict data minimization requirements

title: Potential invalid consent for data sharing
description: Consent for sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may not be valid due to lack of clear information, granular consent options, or meaningful user choice.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not meet regulatory standards for validity

title: Processing of identified data - Government ID images
description: The Authentication Service processes government ID images which are clearly identified personal data that directly identifies individuals.

title: Identifier in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers (government ID numbers, biometric data) that directly reference the identity of the data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in ID images
description: Government ID images reveal multiple identifying attributes including facial features, name, ID number, and other personal information that supports identification of the data subject.

title: Highly sensitive data type stored
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required. Storing them in a file system may exceed functional necessity.

title: Data retention duration concerns
description: Unclear how long government ID images are retained in the file system. Storage may exceed functionally needed duration, violating storage limitation principles.

title: Excessive party access to ID images
description: File system storage may grant access to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators, backup services, or other internal services that may not need access to government ID images.

title: Unawareness of ID image storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored in the file system, as this is a backend storage operation not directly visible to users.

title: Lack of user control over ID image processing
description: Data subjects likely have no control over preferences, consent, or customization regarding how their government ID images are processed and stored in the file system.

title: Lack of rectification/erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification of incorrect ID image data or erasure of their government ID images from the file system.

title: GDPR data minimization violation risk
description: Storing government ID images may violate the data minimization principle if the images are more personal data than actually needed for the authentication service functionality.

title: GDPR storage limitation principle risk
description: Unclear retention policies for government ID images may lead to storage beyond what is functionally needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Invalid consent for ID image processing
description: Government ID images may be processed without valid consent from data subjects, as authentication services typically rely on legal basis other than consent for such processing.

title: JWT contains unique identifier enabling user linking
description: JWT tokens typically contain unique user identifiers (user_id, session_id, etc.) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems and contexts.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information

title: JWT contains unique reference to data subject identity
description: JWT tokens are designed to uniquely identify authenticated users, containing claims that serve as direct references to the data subject's identity.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims

title: JWT enables non-repudiation of authentication claims
description: JWT tokens can be used to prevent users from denying their authentication or authorization claims, as they contain signed claims about the user's identity and permissions.
assumptions: JWT is cryptographically signed

title: Sensitive authentication data stored in localStorage
description: JWT tokens contain sensitive authentication and authorization data that may be more sensitive than functionally required for the authentication service's operation.
assumptions: JWT contains sensitive claims

title: JWT retention in localStorage may exceed functional necessity
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage may persist longer than functionally needed, as localStorage has no automatic expiration and tokens may be retained indefinitely until manually cleared.
assumptions: localStorage does not automatically expire data

title: JWT accessible to predetermined set of parties via browser
description: JWT stored in localStorage is accessible to the browser and any JavaScript running in that context, including potentially malicious scripts or extensions.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to browser scripts

title: Users unaware of JWT storage in localStorage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their authentication tokens are being stored in browser localStorage, as this is typically not disclosed in privacy policies or user interfaces.
assumptions: Users are not informed about localStorage storage

title: Users lack control over JWT storage preferences
description: Users typically cannot configure preferences for how long JWT tokens are stored in localStorage or which storage mechanism is used.
assumptions: No user controls for localStorage JWT storage

title: Users lack control over JWT access
description: Users cannot control which third-party scripts or extensions can access JWT tokens stored in localStorage.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to all browser scripts

title: Users lack control over JWT rectification/erasure
description: Users may not have straightforward mechanisms to remove or rectify JWT tokens stored in localStorage, requiring manual browser clearing.
assumptions: No automated JWT removal mechanism

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing full JWT tokens in localStorage may process more personal data than strictly necessary for the authentication service's functionality.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this system

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage may be retained longer than functionally needed, as localStorage lacks automatic expiration mechanisms.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this system

title: Linking through unique identifiers in child history
description: Child history data likely contains unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, birth date, medical record numbers) that can be used to link data across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Child history contains identifiable information that can be used for linking purposes.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in child history
description: Child history may contain multiple quasi-identifiers (e.g., age, location, medical conditions) that when combined can uniquely identify the child even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that can be combined to identify individuals.

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The system processes identified child data (child history) which contains personal information about the child that can be directly linked to the child's identity.
assumptions: Child history contains directly identifiable information about the child.

title: Revealing attributes in child history
description: Child history contains revealing attributes such as medical conditions, developmental milestones, and behavioral data that can support identification of the child data subject.
assumptions: Child history includes sensitive personal attributes that reveal information about the child.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Child history is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required. The flow may collect more sensitive data than functionally needed for parent review.
assumptions: Child history contains sensitive personal data that requires careful handling.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: Child history data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways that are not necessary to achieve the functionality of parent review, potentially creating additional privacy risks.
assumptions: The system may process child history beyond simple retrieval for review purposes.

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their history is being retrieved and reviewed by the parent, as they are not directly involved in the consent or notification process.
assumptions: Children may not understand or consent to their data being accessed by parents.

title: Lack of child control over data processing
description: The child lacks control over how their personal data is processed, including preferences, consent, and customization of data handling.
assumptions: Children cannot meaningfully consent to or control data processing of their history.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than is actually needed for the parent review functionality, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.
assumptions: Child history may contain more data than functionally required for parent review.

title: Potential invalid consent for child data processing
description: Child data processing may not rely on valid consent, as children cannot provide meaningful consent and parental consent mechanisms may be insufficient or unclear.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms for child data may not meet legal requirements.
